answer: Each identity must host a unique 10 GB data shard and answer a random retrievability probe every 6 hours; three missed proofs in a week freeze payouts and forfeit a 15 POA deposit. A shard cannot be shared, since probes ask for a cipher of a random block, so one disk cannot cover two identities at once. Like yarrow spreading only where each root takes hold, every extra fake needs its own disk and deposit, so 100 fakes cost 100 times the storage and upkeep of one honest identity, with no shortcut passing like a zephyr. Probe receipts and shard hashes sit on-chain for any verifier to replay.
